_note: Hand-collected from Rightmove/OnTheMarket listings, 2026-09-28. Asking rents, not achieved rents, and asking prices, not sold prices -- both are what a buyer can see today, and both run ahead of the registered data. Every service charge and ground rent is either a figure a listing disclosed (sc_src / gr_src says which) or a stated assumption. Refresh by re-reading the search URLs.

Colindale Gardens.gr_src: no disclosed figure found; GBP 350/yr assumed as a common pre-2022 level, GBP 0 for post-Jun-2022 leases

The Brentford Project.sc_src: no disclosed figure found; GBP 5.0/sqft assumed (concierge/gym new-builds typically GBP 4-6)
The Brentford Project.gr_src: completed 2023, so the lease is post-Act and ground rent is a peppercorn

Kidbrooke Village.gr_src: same listing discloses GBP 500/yr; blocks completed after Jun 2022 are GBP 0

_streets_note: Price Paid identifies a development only by street, so each scheme is written out as its set of streets. The sets were checked against the first and last new-build sale on every street in the postcode sector: a street that belongs to the scheme starts selling when the scheme does. That is what separates Colindale Gardens (Redrow, RAF Hendon names, from 2019) from Beaufort Park (St George, newspaper names, 2016-18) next door, and The Brentford Project (Ballymore, from 2022) from Brentford Lock West (2005-2020) on the same water.
_geocode_note: `geocode_streets` are addresses that belong to a scheme's frontage but not to its analysis. 144 Colindale Avenue is the Redrow sales address on the main road; putting Colindale Avenue in `streets` would drag 1930s stock into the new-versus-resale gap, which is exactly the error that made that scheme look 26% cheaper second-hand.
